name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect Changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      src: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.src }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.desktop }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            src:
              - '**'
              - '!.planning/**'
              - '!.learnings/**'
              - '!docs/**'
              - '!designs/**'
              - '!00-Preliminary-R&D/**'
              - '!.claude/**'
              - '!**/*.md'
              - '!LICENSE'
            desktop:
              - 'apps/desktop/**'
              - 'packages/crypto/**'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run linter
        run: pnpm lint

  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run type checker
        run: pnpm typecheck

  api-spec:
    name: Verify API Spec & Client
    needs: [changes]
    if: |
      github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.src == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Generate OpenAPI spec and API client
        run: pnpm api:generate
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          NODE_ENV: test
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080

      - name: Format generated files
        run: |
          pnpm eslint --fix apps/web/src/api/ || true
          pnpm prettier --write packages/api-client/openapi.json apps/web/src/api/

      - name: Verify no uncommitted changes to generated files
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code packages/api-client/openapi.json || (echo "OpenAPI spec is out of date. Run 'pnpm api:generate' and commit changes." && exit 1)
          git diff --exit-code apps/web/src/api/ || (echo "Generated API client is out of date. Run 'pnpm api:generate' and commit changes." && exit 1)

  test:
    name: Test
    needs: [changes, lint, typecheck]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.src == 'true')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run API tests with coverage
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test:cov
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
          NODE_ENV: test
          IPFS_PROVIDER: local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL: http://localhost:8080

      - name: Run Crypto tests with coverage
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto test:coverage

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./apps/api/coverage/lcov.info,./packages/crypto/coverage/lcov.info
          flags: api,crypto
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  build:
    name: Build
    needs: [changes, lint, typecheck, api-spec, test]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.src == 'true')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build packages (excluding desktop)
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto --filter @cipherbox/api --filter @cipherbox/web build

  cargo-check-windows:
    name: Cargo Check (Windows)
    needs: [changes, lint]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install WinFsp
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $out = "winfsp.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","$out","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow

      - name: Create WinFsp MSI placeholder for resource glob
        shell: powershell
        run: New-Item -ItemType File -Force -Path "apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources/winfsp-placeholder.msi"

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: windows-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: windows-cargo-

      - name: Cargo check with winfsp feature
        run: cargo check --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features winfsp

  cargo-check-macos:
    name: Cargo Check (macOS)
    needs: [changes, lint]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install FUSE-T
        run: brew install --cask fuse-t

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: macos-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: macos-cargo-

      - name: Cargo check with fuse feature
        working-directory: apps/desktop/src-tauri
        run: cargo check --no-default-features --features fuse

  build-desktop-windows:
    name: Build Windows Desktop
    needs: [changes, cargo-check-windows, typecheck]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install WinFsp
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $resourceDir = "${{ github.workspace }}/apps/desktop/src-tauri/resources"
          $out = "$resourceDir/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","$out","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: windows-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: windows-cargo-

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build crypto package
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          args: -- --no-default-features --features winfsp

  build-desktop-macos:
    name: Build macOS Desktop
    needs: [changes, cargo-check-macos, typecheck]
    if: |
      !failure() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true')
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install FUSE-T
        run: brew install --cask fuse-t

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: rustup default stable

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            apps/desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: macos-cargo-${{ hashFiles('apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: macos-cargo-

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build crypto package
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          args: -- --no-default-features --features fuse

Here's how this works:

**`src` filter** — added 4 exclusions:
- `!**/package.json` — all package.json files across the monorepo
- `!**/Cargo.toml` — Cargo manifests
- `!**/tauri.conf.json` — Tauri config
- `!.release-please-manifest.json` — Release Please tracking file

**`desktop` filter** — added exclusions inline after each include:
- `!apps/desktop/package.json`, `!apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `!apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — for the `apps/desktop/**` group
- `!packages/crypto/package.json` — for the `packages/crypto/**` group

**Why this is safe:** Version bumps only touch these manifest files. Any real change (new dependency, code change, config change) will also modify other files:
- New npm dependency → `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes → matches `**`
- New Rust dependency → `Cargo.lock` changes → matches `apps/desktop/**`
- Code changes → `.ts`/`.rs` files change → always matched

So a Release Please PR with only version bumps → `src=false`, `desktop=false` → expensive jobs skip. A feature PR that happens to also bump a version → other changed files still trigger CI normally.

chore(ci): exclude version-bump files from change detection

Release Please PRs only update version fields in package.json,
Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json, and .release-please-manifest.json.
These changes don't affect build output, so exclude them from
the paths-filter to avoid triggering expensive CI jobs (Windows/macOS
desktop builds, tests, etc.) on every release PR.

(pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock) which continue to match the filters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1→import { create } from 'zustand';
     2→import type { DeviceRegistry } from '@cipherbox/crypto';
     3→
     4→type DeviceRegistryState = {
     5→  /** The decrypted device registry */
     6→  registry: DeviceRegistry | null;
     7→  /** This device's ID for highlighting in UI */
     8→  currentDeviceId: string | null;
     9→  /** IPNS name for the registry (display/debug) */
    10→  registryIpnsName: string | null;
    11→  /** Unix ms of last successful sync */
    12→  lastSyncedAt: number | null;
    13→  /** Last error message, null = no error */
    14→  syncError: string | null;
    15→  /** True after first successful load/create */
    16→  isInitialized: boolean;
    17→
    18→  // Actions
    19→  setRegistry: (registry: DeviceRegistry, ipnsName: string, deviceId: string) => void;
    20→  updateRegistry: (registry: DeviceRegistry) => void;
    21→  setSyncError: (error: string) => void;
    22→  clearRegistry: () => void;
    23→};
    24→
    25→/**
    26→ * Device registry store for managing encrypted device registry state.
    27→ *
    28→ * Tracks the registry (list of authenticated devices), current device ID,
    29→ * IPNS name, sync status, and initialization state. No sensitive key material
    30→ * is stored here (registry contains only hex-encoded public keys and metadata),
    31→ * but state is still zeroed on clear for clean lifecycle.
    32→ *
    33→ * Used by:
    34→ * - useAuth (sets registry after login, clears on logout)
    35→ * - useDeviceRegistrySync (updates registry on polling)
    36→ * - DeviceApprovalModal + useDeviceApproval (cross-device approval flow)
    37→ */
    38→export const useDeviceRegistryStore = create<DeviceRegistryState>((set) => ({
    39→  // State
    40→  registry: null,
    41→  currentDeviceId: null,
    42→  registryIpnsName: null,
    43→  lastSyncedAt: null,
    44→  syncError: null,
    45→  isInitialized: false,
    46→
    47→  // Actions
    48→  setRegistry: (registry, ipnsName, deviceId) =>
    49→    set({
    50→      registry,
    51→      registryIpnsName: ipnsName,
    52→      currentDeviceId: deviceId,
    53→      syncError: null,
    54→      isInitialized: true,
    55→      lastSyncedAt: Date.now(),
    56→    }),
    57→
    58→  updateRegistry: (registry) =>
    59→    set({
    60→      registry,
    61→      lastSyncedAt: Date.now(),
    62→    }),
    63→
    64→  setSyncError: (error) =>
    65→    set({
    66→      syncError: error,
    67→    }),
    68→
    69→  clearRegistry: () =>
    70→    set({
    71→      registry: null,
    72→      currentDeviceId: null,
    73→      registryIpnsName: null,
    74→      lastSyncedAt: null,
    75→      syncError: null,
    76→      isInitialized: false,
    77→    }),
    78→}));

# Fix MFA Security Tab: Factor Detection, Device Metadata, Recovery Status

## Context

After signing in with a recovery phrase, the Security tab shows three bugs:
1. Device shows "Unknown device" / "last active: unknown" - the factor created during recovery has no metadata
2. Recovery phrase shows "no recovery phrase" - even though it was just used to sign in
3. Factor count (4) is accurate but inconsistent with visible UI (1 device, no recovery shown)

**Root causes** (all traced to Web3Auth SDK internals):

- `enableMFA({})` creates both device and recovery factors with `shareDescription` defaulting to `FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.Other` ("Other"), because the SDK's `createFactor()` defaults to "Other" when no `shareDescription` is provided. Our code only recognizes "deviceShare" and "seedPhrase" types.
- Each factor's stored JSON includes `tssShareIndex` (2=DEVICE, 3=RECOVERY) which can be used to infer the correct type.
- Web3Auth's `addFactorDescription` *spreads* `additionalMetadata` at the top level of the JSON, but our `getFactors()` parser looks for a nested `parsed.additionalMetadata` object that doesn't exist.
- `recoverWithMnemonic()` creates a device factor without any `additionalMetadata` (no `deviceId`, no `browserName`).

## Changes

### 1. Fix `getFactors()` parsing — `apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` (lines 169-202)

- Parse `tssShareIndex` from the flat JSON object
- Normalize type: when `module` is `"Other"`, use `tssShareIndex` to map to correct type:
  - `tssShareIndex === 2` → `FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.DeviceShare`
  - `tssShareIndex === 3` → `FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase`
- Extract metadata fields from the flat JSON structure (not from a nested `additionalMetadata` key)
- Exclude known system fields (`module`, `dateAdded`, `tssShareIndex`) from the extracted metadata

This single change fixes:
- Recovery phrase detection (RecoveryPhraseSection checks `type === 'seedPhrase'`)
- Device list showing enableMFA-created devices (AuthorizedDevices filters on `type === 'deviceShare'`)
- Device names for enableMFA devices (they have `browserName` in top-level metadata set by bowser)

### 2. Add device metadata to recovery flow — `apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` (line 152-158)

In `recoverWithMnemonic()`, add `additionalMetadata` to the `createFactor` call:
```typescript
import { getOrCreateDeviceIdentity } from '../lib/device/identity';
import { detectDeviceInfo } from '../lib/device/info';

// Inside recoverWithMnemonic:
const deviceKeypair = await getOrCreateDeviceIdentity();
const deviceInfo = detectDeviceInfo();

await coreKit.createFactor({
  shareType: TssShareType.DEVICE,
  factorKey: newDeviceFactor.private,
  shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.DeviceShare,
  additionalMetadata: {
    deviceId: deviceKeypair.deviceId,
    browserName: deviceInfo.name,
  },
});
```

This makes the recovery-created device matchable to the device registry for name/lastActive display.

### 3. Fix `enableMfa()` for future enrollments — `apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` (line 84)

Pass `shareDescription` in enableMFA params so the recovery factor gets tagged correctly:
```typescript
const backupFactorKeyHex = await coreKit.enableMFA({
  shareDescription: FactorKeyTypeShareDescription.SeedPhrase,
});
```

The SDK spreads `enableMFAParams` into the recovery factor's `createFactor` call, so this gives future recovery factors the correct "seedPhrase" module. (Existing accounts are handled by fix #1's tssShareIndex normalization.)

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `apps/web/src/hooks/useMfa.ts` | Fix `getFactors()` parsing, add metadata to `recoverWithMnemonic`, fix `enableMfa` params |

No changes needed to `AuthorizedDevices.tsx`, `RecoveryPhraseSection.tsx`, or `SecurityTab.tsx` — the type normalization in `getFactors()` makes downstream consumers work correctly.

## Verification

1. Run `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web dev` pointed at staging API
2. Sign in with recovery phrase
3. Navigate to Settings > Security tab
4. Verify:
   - Recovery phrase shows "recovery phrase active" (not "no recovery phrase")
   - Device list shows current device with browser name (not "Unknown device")
   - If stale device exists, it appears in the list with its browser name and can be revoked
   - Factor count is consistent with visible factors
